item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) Typowriter
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: Highly powerful reality bender manifesting in the form of a common typewriter. The typewriter will essentially create "transcripts" of nearby media, although it often makes typos. If a typo happens to create a sentence in the transcript that grammatically makes sense, it will become reality. It runs forever and will make increasingly more typos on a transcript if the same piece of media is shown to it multiple times.

Central Narrative: I plan for this to be an SCP that has been in containment for awhile, however without any reliable containment procedures. There will be an extensive list of research notes and observations about the operations of SCP XXXX. The main "narrative" stems from a recovered journal. The SCP is contained by singing up 4 unwitting rural towns to use their local news stations, newspapers, and radio broadcasts for SCP XXXX. Although MTFs patrol all 4 towns constantly, one woman begins to keep a journal of all the weird alterations that happen, so she can be sure she isn't going crazy (as the towns are frequently amnestizied due to the SCP)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Completely random reality bender that is able to warp anything by writing a typo

Additional Notes: The reality anchors do not work on this SCP, in actuality because it kills some of the fun associated with it. I think a decent theory within the narrative as to why this is so is that SCP XXXX is a recovered byproduct of SCP 3812 (SCP-3812)

item.title: Re: SCP idea: Nightmare Pillow
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Nobody knows how the pillow determines who falls into a coma and who has a dream, or if the selection is random.

This is fine in universe but is there a like out of universe logic to it? Narratively, what does this split effect actually add here? Like, why does it make the idea more interesting than just having folk lucid dream on it?

Central Narrative

My concern with this section as a whole is 'the foundation tries to figure out what is happening' feels like it might be underwhelming as a story, particularly in a SCP article if you lead with a description saying it's the pillow. Theoretically you could get around this by calling it a provisional SCP file in need of updating say; but it feels like there's not a lot of interesting plot beats happening during this investigation?

You mention a line in the Hook section that I think needs to be explored more here:

It’s currently unknown as to where the railroad goes, or if the entities within the dreams have any significance.

Like, investigating whether the railroad goes somewhere and the significance of the entities within the dream feels like a good framework to build a story off, particularly if you focussed in on a single dreamer and made the answers to these feel personally significant to them.

I'm a little unsure about your choice of object here: a pillow that makes you dream feels…somewhat cliche? Like it's very much the obvious anomalous effect for a pillow to have; and stuff that affects your dreams is relatively well trod on the wiki (see e.g. The Oneiroi Collective GoI or the 145 SCPs tagged with sleep); and so you're really going to have to do more narratively with this than just 'ooo weird dreams', y'know?

item.title: Room for potential, but misses in the end.
item.content:encoded:

I like the concept, but I feel like it was developed the wrong way/didn't explore everything.

  • Containment doesn't take into account that "SCP-4663 is capable of consuming all inorganic substances". (Unanswered Question)
  • SCP-4663-1 instances are alive even though they're made from thread that is created from inorganic substances? I don't think this really adds much except as an excuse to not experiment on SCP-4663-1 using 3D-printer-based experiments. (Doesn't Make Sense + Unanswered Question)
  • "physical changes and evolutions happen frequently," This feels more like an excuse for the Addendum which doesn't really add to the article since it's just random. What of the old SCP-4663 instances? I feel that an experiment/test log would be more appropriate than the Addendum, though that alone might not improve the overall article. (Doesn't Make Sense + Unanswered Question + Engagement Difficulty)
  • Even if you keep the Addendum, it pokes at a "what-if" that's not further explored. Maybe a post-incident report or purposefully recreating the incident in a controlled environment? (Unanswered Question + Engagement Difficulty)

Currently a 4/10
no vote

item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) The Abnormal High School
item.content:encoded:
1) You can have a meteor hit by a nuclear missile, not an asteroid. However, even if a meteor was hit by a nuke, it wouldn't likely end up as radioactive.

2) There already a couple of high schools and anomalous student organizations. There are even a couple of reconstructed buildings. I'm not sure combining them makes for an interesting idea. It just feels like this is the beginning of an idea and needs to be seriously fleshed out. You also need to shy away from an X-Men school.

3) The "Hook/Attention Grabber" needs to be a reason why people are interested in the SCP, not just more history. This is the best place to describe why we would be interested in the SCP, and what it offers as unique compared to other SCPs, especially those that are similar.

Bon chance!

item.title: Seeking greenlight: burden caused by a simple birthmark
item.content:encoded:
A birthmark which seems to make anyone around mess with you, EXCEPT ONE person.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Elevator Pitch: An instance wherein a person bears a birthmark. And if someone has this birthmark, anyone he/she knew and/or people he/she encounters mess up with him. This instance occurs randomly in any person living anywhere in the world. The effect starts immediately upon birth.

Central Narrative: the existence of this scp has tipped off the foundation through a field agent who reports that a certain teen has been bullied on, messed upon, and abused and was left by his parents and relatives alone to live for himself. It also reported that it was all caused by his birthmark on the back. At first the foundation laughed this off and didn't believe the agent. So he just investigates this on his own.
investigation results and the occurrences of certain incidents has finally convinced the foundation and authorized for monitoring of possible instances of this scp, and further investigation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
You might see some commentary on bullying or something related since this scp was inspired at it. This depicts an emotion felt by someone that was not accepted by the society because of something the he/she has.

Additional Notes:
An scp that causes it's host to be picked off by the people around him/her, except for a certain person who, in despite of the person's comfort, love and support, still picked of and messed upon by the people around.

item.title: Re: Parasitic Amoeba
item.content:encoded:
1) If you want this to be an end-of-the-world scenario, then the amoebae needs to have a way of spreading and doing so fast. Going after poor people is not the best ticket to do that. Also, there's the question of how it would survive basic purification practices (large containers frequently use tablets every so often in order to keep infectants like bacteria and mold from becoming a problem; amoebae would be included in that due to the danger of dysentery, which is caused by them).

2) The Foundation needs to be included in this somehow. If this is solely something that happens on the periphery and no one has heard of it, then that means that neither has The Foundation and it, therefore, wouldn't be in their catalog.

3) There's also way too much mystery on this. Remember: Less is more. A mysterious stranger that disappears when he dumps something into a container and has the ability to paralyze people is a lot of steps too far here. A mysterious stranger dumping stuff when no one is around and only getting caught as a glimpse in a security camera is a lot more effective (and also gives The Foundation something to put into a case file).

Even if the figure is a humanoid amoeba (which would be a fun twist), it needs to act within the limits of such (such as leaving clothes behind when it de-manifests) in order to be scary. It should maybe also leave behind some sort of mucous.

4) While it's always interesting to see a new disease-based anomaly, this one has a lot of work. You may want to do some research on dysentery (a more rapid form would work well here, especially if it targets specific organs and causes them to shut down far more rapidly than normal).


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Parasitic Amoeba

I'm generally of two minds on this. Yes, the story is in there somewhere. It might even be a pretty nice story. Unfortunately, it is both too distant and not initially interesting enough to get me invested. I'm not saying every story needs to be fully explored of course. I just didn't feel like this one gave me enough of an initial investment for me to feel gratified in searching for the rest.
That, and a lot of the dialogue feels pretty clunky to me.

Here's an example:

I think she said something, but I took off running, so I don't remember exactly what her exact words, but…

That's a very difficult sentence to read. I know it's spoken dialogue, so it doesn't have to be grammatically perfect, but it helps to be enjoyable to read.

item.title: [Feedback request] Enigma Dilemma
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Unsure, guidance requested

Elevator Pitch: An 18th century naval war table that displays the location of every military vessel currently on water in the world.

Central Narrative: The war table is suspected to have been made during the American Revolution*, leading to many of the naval battles of the war ending in British defeat despite their superiority on sea. It is also thought to have been used in the battles of Manila Bay (1898) and Coronel (1914), as well as many decisive (and unlikely) engagements in WWII. Following the war, the object was considered displaced and eventually lost until resurfacing in the continental US some 50 years later. Through unclear means, it had ended up in an antique shop where its outrageous price had scared off any buyers for years until the Foundation's involvement.

*the nature of the Battle of Quiberon Bay in 1759 has raised concerns regarding the object's assumed creation date.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The title of this thread: an Enigma dilemma. In WWII, Britain cracked the Enigma cipher. However, using this to save every Allied naval convoy from U-boats would have made it obvious to the Germans that their cipher has been cracked, and so Allied command was faced with a question: you know where, what, and when the enemy will strike. Which attacks do you let happen and which attacks do you thwart?

This SCP is a similar question but on a far larger scale; every public, secret, and clandestine naval movement is laid bare. Any naval force secretly moving against another would force the international, humanity-shielding Foundation to either pick sides, or let conflict after conflict happen. With what could happen if it fell into the wrong hands, and with GOIs interested in acquiring the object, securing, containing, and protecting is very literal.

Additional Notes: This would be my first contribution to the site and as such, I would appreciate thorough criticism. There are currently no drafts and I am not counting on this being approved or greenlit, though that would be a nice surprise. Additionally, I'd like some help with the genres—or is History alone enough?


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
I've lifted the footnote for the Central Narrative out of the collapsible. I hope this is alright. Amarrat.

item.title: Re: A helping hand (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
1) If it can't be contained and it doesn't appear to be controlled by any stretch, how were they able to test it? Also, if it teleports, why wouldn't the tracker fall off when it teleported? They must have had some incredible reflexes to have tagged it.

2) Setting it at "Keter" may be a little high; I get that it can't be contained, but it's also relatively safe. I could see "Euclid" due to how hard it is to contain, but I'm not sure it's that dangerous.

3) Given that it's just a hand, does it have a limit on how much it can lift? This would affect its usefulness, as well as its ability to wield weapons. Also, how often is it helping?

[Obligatory: I'm seeing parallels between this and the D&D spell "mage hand", which has a limit of about 5 pounds. While it doesn't need to apply here, it does make for an obvious question.]

4) If the hand is making no pains to remain hidden, how is it avoiding having a presence on social media? Assuming it's helping as often as it can, or even as rarely as once a week, it would develop some sort of following.

5) Overall, it's a great idea and it's nice to see a more positive anomaly. It just needs to be a little more detailed.

item.title: SCP idea- Plant a page and what's written on it will grow.
item.content:encoded:
A book that when you write something on a page and plant the page, it will grow into a tree and fruit what was written on it.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Use of extensive test logs and interviews

Elevator Pitch: Its an old notebook found with blank pages that when you write something on one of the pages and plant the page a tree grows and will fruit what's written on the page. The only limits is that what's written is that it must be a tangible item, the item is not fictitious, and the writer knows/has seen what they're writing about. In the event that item written does not fruit, the a paper with the written word will fruit instead. The fruited item will be identical to what was written but will taste, smell, and decay like an apple. Pages are replenished when closing the book.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: Exploration of the uses and loopholes such as: creating a sapient being, creating existing SCPs, creating additional D class personnel, creating confinement cells, intention over what's written, and duplications of itself.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Creative potential of what can be made, some interviews with the sapient creations who may or may not experience existential crises, and showing ideas of self image. The tone is slightly comedic with how discoveries of loopholes are made.

Additional Notes: This is my first SCP and first work of creative writing that I have done in a very long time. I am unsure to how in-depth I should go with the test logs, whether this a creative enough concept, or if something like this already exists.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique

It's a wish-fulfilling humanoid bug person. That in and of itself could have led to something interesting and meaningful if this concept went anywhere with it. Instead, we got an extremely short test log with the only personality being, 'I like to eat larva and I need good sleep.'

While reading this, I got the absolute barebones feeling this thing had the a childlike innocence, but it was so minimal, it didn't matter in the end.

Apologies if this is harsh. -1.

item.title: A rare find
item.content:encoded:
I've always liked the articles or tales that delve into ethics or philosophy and this is a rare find. It takes a modern ethical dilemma and uses the setting of the SCP Universe to help its "argument" as well as use the ethical dilemma itself to show the underworkings of life for a D-Class at the Foundation.

  • A D-Class reforming himself, understanding what he and the Foundation have done for the world and the lives that have been secretly saving.
  • A look into how the Foundation's "cold utilitarianism" doesn't mean cold people. Some people get mentally crushed by what they do at the Foundation while others accept what they do for the greater good.
  • An argument against the "cycle of vengeance" and why killing isn't the right choice.

It's rare to find an article so strongly based around an ethical dilemma that's both an ethical argument AND provides lore for the SCP Universe. +1

item.title: Creature that thinks it's a nanny
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch:

  • An entity that refers to itself as the Nanny.
  • capable of producing a thick fog around it. Lives in a marshland in the south of England.
  • It tries to lure people towards it with glowing globules of light. Once a person reaches it, it will proceed to ask them to tea, to play some games or have their medicine (other things as well). Keeps the person captive performing perversions of nanny-care. For example, feeding someone their medicine might be pushing mud into their mouth or giving them tea might be feeding them mud and rocks. It essentially tries to immobilise them under the ruse of caring for them.
  • Once they have been deemed to have sufficiently cared for, the nanny takes them to a place it refers to as 'the garden' (is a recession in the ground with various pods and bulbs hanging on the walls) there it introduces them to the 'other children' which appear to be larvae or younglings of this creature who then devour the human.

Central Narrative: D-class sent into the marsh, discover the nanny and are brought to the garden, try escaping. Reveals other ability of the SCP, has full control over the location, temperature and density of the fog around it. Used to help catch prey or defend itself.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: An entity that lures people with lights sort of like an angler fish, also similar to will'o'wisps which could explain the folklore in that area.

Additional Notes: NONE

item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) The Bartender
item.content:encoded:
This isn't really dong it for me. While I don't usually mind it when something just happens for no real reason (anomalous phenomena don't really need much of an explanation as to why or how they happen, because that would defeat the purpose of it, after all), I find this to be lacking in a steady logical thread to follow.

From what I gather, going from the start, an early 20th century boy grows up with a dream to bar tend in New Orleans, is driven to a boiling point by his father, dies in a car accident, and then assumes the form of a nightmarish entity. And then the Foundation has them in custody. It feels like there is some missing gaps here and a want for the entity to be powerful. Not saying that the entity can't be a powerful nightmarish freak, but if that's what you want, then focusing on this shallow origin story isn't the way to go.

I know you have a draft ready, but to be honest, I don't think it would change my mind much. What I would suggest based on the summary of the concept here is re-evaluating what exactly you want to see this article grow into. If you want a creature with a sad story, then some work is going to have to go into making the story impactful and relevant to the creature's current state. If you want to make a super monster, consider how you could best showcase that monster's cunning and strength and couple it with how the Foundation interacts with it.

item.title: Glad That I Decided to Keep Reading
item.content:encoded:
When I first started reading this, I was like "yeah, a gold man that you eat, and you get gold delivered, and then the Foundation gets mean, and takes it away. Meh."

And then I started reading the transcripts, and I couldn't help but upvote.

A lot of might be cliché and tropified (the car chase, the O5 council fighting over the Goldman), but then again, I don't mind cliché if done right. And I found a lot of the humor to be rather cheeky.

The guy with a chainsaw and going "Timbeeeer!" was just classic, and helps set the tone! And I have to agree with Raptie. The line "Aye… want to eat that gold man" was just brilliant!

The repeating fight between the O5 council comes off as a bit repetitive by the third incarnation, but the listing of a different set of weapons (apparently standard for the Foundation, though what the heck Switchback Energy Grenades, Zoological Grenades, Reverse Matter Railguns, and Occult Pistols and Rifles are supposed to is sadly still a mystery) was also interesting. And apparently, they also have farm animals scurrying around headquarters now…

Having O5-4 dive through Alpha-1-5's legs was pretty funny, but I think that visually, having a couple of other O5's accidentally run into him like in Home Alone 2 would be hilarious!

item.title: Re: Real Life Publishing Opportunities
item.content:encoded:
Diabolical Plots is opening their submissions window for the entire month of January 2021. Submission guidelines here. They are seeking science fiction, fantasy, and horror with speculative elements with a firm limit of 3500 words. They pay 10c/word and are a SFWA-qualifying market.

WHAT ARE WE LOOKING FOR?
Speculative fiction–science fiction, fantasy, and horror. Everything should have a speculative element–that includes horror. Feel free to mix in other genres at will–a fantasy mystery or a science fiction romance.

And yes, we really mean it has to have a speculative element. If you submit a serial killer story with only mundane elements, even though that could be a horror story it’s not a speculative horror story and it will be rejected regardless of quality.

Things that we tend to really like:
Weird fiction
Sense of wonder
Strong character and plot arcs
Strong worldbuilding, hinting at more to see around the edges of the story
Philosophical food-for-thought
Straightforward, easily readable style
Religion, where the story does not try to convert the reader, nor does the story demonize religion
Platonic friendship between men and women

item.title: SCP idea- Plant a page and what what's written on it will grow.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Use of extensive test logs and interviews

Elevator Pitch: Its an old notebook found with blank pages that when you write something on one of the pages and plant the page a tree grows and will fruit what's written on the page. The only limits is that what's written is that it must be a tangible item, the item is not fictitious, and the writer knows/has seen what they're writing about. In the event that item written does not fruit, the a paper with the written word will fruit instead. The fruited item will be identical to what was written but will taste, smell, and decay like an apple. Pages are replenished when closing the book.

Central Narrative: Exploration of the uses and loopholes such as: creating a sapient being, creating existing SCPs, creating additional D class personnel, creating confinement cells, intention over what's written, and duplications of itself.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Creative potential of what can be made and some interviews with existential crises from the sapient creations an well as ideas of self image. The tone is slightly comedic with how discoveries of loopholes are made.

Additional Notes: This is my first SCP and first work of creative fiction that I have done in a very long time. I am unsure to how in-depth I should go with the test logs or even whether this a creative enough concept.
